definition: A tensor product network, in artificial neural networks, is a network that exploits the properties of tensors to model associative concepts such as variable assignment.
details: Orthonormal vectors are chosen to model the ideas (such as variable names and target assignments), and the tensor product of these vectors construct a network whose mathematical properties allow the user to easily extract the association from it.

explainer.lead: A tensor product network is an artificial neural network that exploits tensor properties to model associative concepts such as variable assignment. It matters because its mathematical structure allows associations to be extracted easily rather than learned implicitly.

tiers.eli5: Think of pairing a name tag with a value by binding them together, so later you can pull the pair apart and read what belongs to what.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose orthonormal vectors for variable names and target assignments, then bind them via tensor products. The pitfall is that the binding is only recoverable if the chosen vectors stay orthonormal.
tiers.paperLevel: Orthonormal vectors model ideas such as variable names and assignments; the tensor product of these vectors constructs a network whose properties allow extraction of the association. Correct extraction depends on orthonormality.

explainer.example: A network binds a vector for the variable name with a vector for its assigned value via a tensor product; the stored assignment is later read back out of the network.
